items.fact: Loss = error for one datapoint; cost = aggregate (usually mean); used interchangeably
items.where: Reading, Terms, first bullet

items.fact: Choice driven by the dependent variable: numeric -> regression, probabilistic -> classification
items.where: Reading, Terms, second bullet; In one screen table

items.fact: CE = negative log likelihood of the correct class; minimising CE is MLE
items.where: Reading, Terms, third bullet (plus MSE as Gaussian MLE, MAE as Laplace)

items.fact: MSE formula (y - yhat)^2
items.where: Reading, regression table; Loss shapes

items.fact: MSE pro: smooth gradient that shrinks near the minimum, clean convergence for small errors
items.where: Reading, regression table, MSE 'For'

items.fact: MSE con: squaring makes huge errors dominate, drastic update jumps, very outlier-sensitive
items.where: Reading, regression table, MSE 'Against'; outlier animation

items.fact: RMSE = sqrt(MSE)
items.where: Reading, regression table

items.fact: RMSE pro: same units as target
items.where: Reading, regression table, RMSE 'For'

items.fact: RMSE pro: 'less extreme than MSE for large errors, still more outlier-sensitive than MAE'
items.where: Corrected in the RMSE row: same minimiser as MSE, so exactly as outlier-sensitive when trained on; it is only as a reported number that it is in target units

items.fact: RMSE con: 'linear scoring, so gradient does not soften near the minimum'
items.where: Corrected and kept in the RMSE row: RMSE's gradient u_i/(N RMSE) does not shrink as all errors shrink together (derived); 'linear scoring' belongs to MAE and is carried in the MAE row

items.fact: MAE row (formula |y - yhat|; pros and cons garbled in the Notion export)
items.where: Reading, regression table MAE row, rebuilt: every point pulls with the same force, outliers that are real data cannot dominate, estimates the median; gradient does not soften near the minimum

items.fact: MAPE row (formula |y - yhat|/|y|; pros and cons garbled in the export)
items.where: Reading, regression table MAPE row, rebuilt: scale-free; no value at y = 0, huge near it; biased low (Gneiting 2011); MAPE section with sklearn's documented behaviour

items.fact: Huber row: quadratic for |e| <= delta, linear beyond (pros and cons garbled)
items.where: Reading, regression table Huber row with Huber 1964 formula; MSE near the target, MAE far; delta in target units; second derivative 0 beyond delta; leverage correction

items.fact: Log-cosh formula log cosh(y - yhat)
items.where: Reading, regression table; Loss shapes

items.fact: Log-cosh pro: Huber-shaped but twice differentiable (XGBoost-style second-order methods)
items.where: Reading, regression table and the 'Two claims about log-cosh, checked' box (half right: its second derivative also decays to 0)

items.fact: Log-cosh pro: cheaper than Huber
items.where: Corrected in the 'Two claims about log-cosh' box: not in arithmetic

items.fact: Log-cosh con: fixed scale, no delta to adapt to the data
items.where: Reading, regression table; demonstrated on the rivers picker (log-cosh = median in miles)

items.fact: Rule of thumb: MSE by default, MAE/Huber when outliers are real data, log-cosh when a second derivative is needed
items.where: Reading, paragraph after the regression table

items.fact: Label smoothing: 1 - eps on true class and eps/(K-1) elsewhere; overconfident models, calibration
items.where: Reading, classification table, both conventions side by side (PyTorch and Szegedy use eps/K mixing)

items.fact: Weighted CE: per-class weight, upweight minority class
items.where: Reading, classification table (plus PyTorch's mean divides by summed weights)

items.fact: Focal loss: -(1 - p_t)^gamma log p_t, extreme imbalance, dense detection, down-weights easy examples
items.where: Reading, classification table and focal paragraph; Loss shapes
